intro: This site makes a lot of claims. This page says where each kind of claim comes from, which parts are measurement and which are judgement, and where it is most likely to be wrong. Nothing here is hidden behind a methodology PDF — the same JSON files that render the site render this page, so it cannot drift out of date relative to what you are reading.

reading.def: One layer of the stack. There are 27, ordered by physical depth — 01 is rock in the ground, 27 is everything the chain leaves behind. The ordering is a claim about dependency, not about importance.

A distinct technology, process or market inside a stratum, with its own physics and its own incumbents. There are 131. A station is drawn where an engineer would recognise a boundary, not where an analyst would.

The coloured pips on a card, 0–3. Three magenta pips means a genuine single point of failure for the whole industry. This is a hand-assigned judgement about concentration and substitutability — it is the most subjective number on the site and it is not derived from data.

A directed link meaning this station cannot function without that one. There are 356. They are written from physical and commercial necessity, not from filings or co-mention — which is why the graph knows things no filing-derived dataset does.

A company, institute or state body operating at a station. There are 533 across 40+ jurisdictions. Lists are illustrative of who matters at each link — they are not exhaustive, not ranked, and not a market-share estimate.

provenance.detail: Structure, ordering, prose and the choice of where one station ends and the next begins. Informed by public technical literature, earnings calls and vendor documentation, but the taxonomy itself is an editorial claim.

A 0–3 read on how concentrated and how substitutable each link is. No formula. Where a computed concentration measure is later added, both will be shown side by side rather than one replacing the other.

356 edges asserting physical and commercial necessity. Validated for structural soundness on every build — no orphan references, no self-loops, every station reachable — but soundness is not correctness.
Compiled from company disclosures, trade press and technical literature. Illustrative rather than exhaustive; inclusion is a claim that an organisation matters at that link, not that it leads it.
Capacities, purities, shares and dates from public reporting through mid-2026. These move fast. Treat them as of that vintage, not as live data.

Google's 2025 disclosure gives 0.24 Wh and 0.26 mL for a median Gemini text prompt on a comprehensive basis, against 0.10 Wh counting active accelerators only. Epoch AI places per-output-token energy across roughly two orders of magnitude by model class.
Per-cm² industry figures for ultra-pure water and electricity, scaled to a 300 mm wafer. Industry averages across nodes, not leading-edge specific — likely conservative for the most advanced fabs.

Die counts, reticle limits, transistor counts and HBM stack configurations from vendor documentation. Individual HBM die areas are bounded by the published 11 × 11 mm package rather than disclosed directly.

The 36 objects on the Ruler, from the silicon lattice to the Earth. Each carries its own precision flag — exact for defined or measured quantities, typical for a representative production value that varies by vendor and node, approx for the right order of magnitude. Proportions on the Ruler are true; only the shapes are schematic.

provenance.who: Company site pages, public planning records and trade press
provenance.detail: 56 locations, each carrying its own precision flag — sited where the operator itself publishes the location, approx where it is reconstructed from public reporting, area where the point is the centre of a district rather than a building. Nothing is more precise than the operator has made public, and nothing is derived from imagery, filings or any other private source. The radius attached to each site is the extent of the park, district or campus as publicly described; it is not a claim about the buildings inside it.

A four-way reading of who writes the leading-edge tool controls, who has adopted equivalent ones, who is a restricted destination and who sits outside the perimeter. Export-control law is national, layered and frequently amended; this is an editorial summary of where a site sits in that structure, not a legal determination, and it should not be relied on for any compliance purpose.

provenance.class: Blast radius on the Faults page
provenance.detail: Remove a station and walk every edge downstream. The result is reach: the set of stations that depend on the removed one somewhere up their chain. It is arithmetic over the same traversal the Web lights its supply cones with, and it is not a claim about damage — a link with enormous reach and three suppliers is a nuisance, and a link with modest reach and no substitute is a decade.

For each scenario, a reading of which downstream links have a credible substitute and roughly how long qualifying it takes, and which have none on any timescale worth calling a response. Lead times are years to real volume, not to first sample. The build enforces that a declared consequence names a station the graph actually connects to the removal, and that no scenario classifies its entire blast radius — on most of them the large majority is left explicitly unclassified, which is the honest size of what this reading does not claim to know.

provenance.who: Primary papers, patents and vendor announcements
provenance.detail: 68 capabilities, each with the year it was first demonstrated and the year it reached volume. Where possible the first date cites the paper or patent itself rather than a history of it. Both dates are judgement calls at the margin — science arrives over several years and 'volume' is a matter of where the line is drawn — so each entry carries a confidence: dated where a specialist would recognise both years, contested where one of them is arguable by several. Four entries have no shipping date and are not given one.

provenance.class: What each capability was waiting for
provenance.detail: A five-way reading of why the gap between working and shipping was as long as it was — unfinished science, a missing machine, an incumbent that was cheaper, a scale that did not exist yet, or nobody who wanted it. It is the most interpretive field on the site after criticality, and the finding that three of the twelve longest waits were waiting on the science rests entirely on it. A well-informed reader will reclassify several.

1:50m physical land and admin-0 boundaries, public domain, simplified for this site with a per-ring tolerance and rounded to about a kilometre. Boundaries are drawn for orientation and are Natural Earth's rendering of them, not a position on any of them. Regenerated by scripts/world.mjs, which re-decodes what it wrote and fails if a single coordinate has drifted.

Wafer mass from area × thickness × density. Polysilicon consumption from kerf and ingot crop. Quartzite from the SiO₂ : Si mass ratio and assumed process yields. Every derivation is written out in full behind the relevant step in the Cascade.

limits.title: Criticality is a judgement, not a measurement
limits.body: The pips are the most influential and least defensible numbers on the site. They shape which stations look alarming and which look routine. They come from reading, not from data, and a well-informed reader will disagree with several of them.

limits.title: Company lists are illustrative
limits.body: 533 organisations sounds comprehensive and is not. Whole categories of supplier are represented by two or three names. Absence from a list means nothing; presence means only that the organisation is worth knowing about at that link.

limits.title: The Cascade's central case is a configuration, not an average
limits.body: It describes one plausible way of serving one kind of request on one class of hardware. It is not an industry mean, and multiplying it by global token volume would be a mistake. The ranges shown are the span between defensible parameter choices, not statistical confidence intervals.

limits.title: Fab figures are industry averages
limits.body: Water and electricity per wafer come from cross-industry data spanning many nodes. A leading-edge logic fab is plausibly worse than the average and a mature analog fab plausibly better. The chain treats them as one number because a better public one does not exist.

limits.title: The Faults page has no coupling and no inventory
limits.body: Every dependency in the corpus is present or absent. In reality some are fatal and some are an inconvenience, and nothing here distinguishes them — a station that would lose ten per cent of its output looks identical to one that would stop. There is no inventory either: a shock absorbed by six months of stock renders the same as one absorbed by nothing. And the unit is the station, which is sometimes coarser than the event — a neon interruption is not the loss of all industrial gases. Where that mismatch matters the scenario says so in its own words, but the picture on screen does not.

limits.title: The Lag chart is a sample, not a census
limits.body: Sixty-eight capabilities were chosen because they illustrate something. The industry contains thousands. Every statistic on that page — the medians, the count of thirty-year waits, the claim that only three of them were waiting on the science — is a property of this selection and would move if the selection moved. Nothing was excluded for having an inconvenient lag, but nothing was systematically included either, and a survivorship problem is built in: capabilities that never shipped at all mostly do not appear, because nobody writes their history.

limits.title: A site is not a capacity
limits.body: The Atlas draws where things are, at the extent their operators describe. It says nothing about how much each site produces, and a large park with modest output looks identical to a small one carrying a node. The claim that the leading-edge sites enclose about 170 km² is a claim about ground, not about wafers — treat it as a statement of how little space this industry occupies, not of how much any one circle matters.

limits.title: Everything is mid-2026 vintage
limits.body: Capacities, roadmap dates, ownership and export-control regimes in this field change on a scale of months. Nothing on this site is live. Where a figure has a date attached, believe the date.

limits.title: This is not investment advice
limits.body: No recommendations, no price targets, no view on any security. The site is built as a map for understanding, not a database of record and not a basis for a trade.

corrections.body: The corpus is hand-curated and certainly contains errors. Corrections are the single most valuable contribution — a wrong figure, a missing organisation, a dependency that does not actually hold, a chokepoint that has quietly been resolved. Open an issue with a source and it will be fixed and credited.
